info.title: cantrip - tools for the Cantrip DSL
info.description: The cantrip command-line tool: validate, lint, test and describe Cantrip content, and try statements in a REPL.

options.name: --filter
options.description: only run tests whose name contains <text>

options.name: --trace
options.description: print the causality trace, with any log output, for failing tests

options.name: --name
options.description: only scenarios whose name contains <text>

options.name: --runs
options.description: play each scenario N times, whatever its `runs` line says

options.name: --seed
options.description: the first seed (default 1); runs use S, S+1, ...

options.name: --bot
options.description:
cautious, patient, random, or both (default both, which is cautious and
patient; two bots take about twice as long as one)

options.name: --turn-limit
options.description: turns one battle may take before the run counts as a stall (default 50)

options.name: --watch
options.description:
play one run of one scenario with the first bot, printing every turn, play
and statement
exit codes: 0 success, 1 content errors, failing tests, a run that threw, a battle that hit the
turn limit or a failed expectation (or lint warnings, with --warnings-as-errors), 2 bad usage

options.name: --suppress
options.description:
comma-separated diagnostic codes to leave out, e.g. CT306,CT310, or CT301
for verbs your game registers in C#. Errors from loading always show

options.name: --warnings-as-errors
options.description: lint only: exit with 1 when there are warnings, as for errors

commands.name: lint
commands.description: load content and run static checks

commands.name: repl
commands.description: load content and run DSL statements interactively
